mcqs.stem: Best guess: in what order are §179, bonus depreciation, and regular MACRS applied?

choices.explanation: Correct. §179 reduces basis first; bonus applies to the remainder; MACRS to what's left.

mcqs.explanation: §179 reduces basis first; bonus applies to the remainder; MACRS to what's left.

mcqs.stem: For 2025 the §179 limit is $2,500,000, reduced dollar for dollar once qualifying property placed in service exceeds $4,000,000. A business places $4,300,000 of equipment in service in 2025. What is its maximum §179 deduction (ample income)?

choices.explanation: That's the pre-2025 limit, before indexing.

mcqs.explanation: P.L. 119-21: $2,500,000 limit reduced by purchases over $4,000,000.
mcqs.reviewNote: Uses a One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21) amount or effective date. Verify against current IRS guidance and exam materials.

mcqs.stem: Which statement about the §179 business income limit is true?

choices.explanation: Correct. §179(b)(3): the deduction can't exceed taxable income from active trades or businesses; excess carries forward.

choices.text: The limit also applies to bonus depreciation
§179 can create a net operating loss
choices.explanation: It's limited to business taxable income.

mcqs.explanation: §179(b)(3): the deduction can't exceed taxable income from active trades or businesses; excess carries forward.

mcqs.stem: A 5-year asset costing $50,000 is placed in service in May 2025. The owner elects out of bonus and doesn't use §179. Half-year convention applies. What is 2025 depreciation?

choices.explanation: Uses the second-quarter mid-quarter rate (25%). The mid-quarter convention applies only when more than 40% of the year's depreciable basis is placed in service in the fourth quarter; the stem says half-year applies.

mcqs.explanation: 200% DB, 5-year, half-year → 20% in year 1.

mcqs.stem: Equipment acquired and placed in service in March 2025 (after January 19). What bonus depreciation percentage applies absent an election out?

choices.explanation: That's for property acquired before January 20, 2025.
Correct. P.L. 119-21 restored 100% bonus for property acquired after January 19, 2025.

mcqs.explanation: P.L. 119-21 restored 100% bonus for property acquired after January 19, 2025.
mcqs.reviewNote: Uses a One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21) amount or effective date. Verify against current IRS guidance and exam materials.

mcqs.stem: A business with $80,000 of business taxable income (before §179) elects $120,000 of §179 expense. What is the 2025 deduction?

choices.explanation: Correct. §179 is limited to business taxable income; the excess carries forward.

mcqs.explanation: §179 is limited to business taxable income; the excess carries forward.

mcqs.stem: A nonresidential building (cost $3,900,000, excluding land) is placed in service on January 5. Using straight-line over 39 years with the mid-month convention, what is year-1 depreciation?
mcqs.explanation: Placed in service in January → 11.5 months: 3,900,000 ÷ 39 × 11.5 ÷ 12 = 95,833.

mcqs.stem: A car is used 40% for business. Which method is required?

choices.explanation: Correct. §280F(b): listed property with 50% or less business use must use ADS.

mcqs.explanation: §280F(b): listed property with 50% or less business use must use ADS.

mcqs.stem: A company buys a business and allocates $600,000 to goodwill on July 1, 2025. What is the 2025 amortization?

choices.explanation: Doesn't prorate for the partial year.

mcqs.explanation: §197: 15-year straight-line from the month acquired (6 months in 2025).

mcqs.stem: A new business incurs $53,000 of start-up costs and begins operations on April 1, 2025. What is the 2025 deduction?
mcqs.explanation: Immediate deduction 5,000 − 3,000 = 2,000; amortize 51,000 ÷ 180 × 9 months = 2,550; total 4,550.

mcqs.stem: A calendar-year corporation pays $500,000 of domestic research wages in 2025. How is the cost treated?

choices.explanation: That was the 2022–2024 rule for domestic R&E.
Correct. P.L. 119-21 added §174A: domestic research is deductible for tax years beginning after 2024.

choices.text: Capitalized with no recovery until disposal

mcqs.explanation: P.L. 119-21 added §174A: domestic research is deductible for tax years beginning after 2024.
mcqs.reviewNote: Uses a One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21) amount or effective date. Verify against current IRS guidance and exam materials.

mcqs.stem: Which statement correctly contrasts §179 with bonus depreciation?

choices.text: Both are limited to the business's taxable income for the year
§179 can create or increase an NOL
Bonus depreciation has an annual dollar cap
§179 is asset by asset; bonus opt-out is by class
choices.explanation: Correct. §179 offers asset-by-asset flexibility within dollar and income limits; bonus is class-wide and unlimited.

mcqs.explanation: §179 offers asset-by-asset flexibility within dollar and income limits; bonus is class-wide and unlimited.

mcqs.stem: A company placed 7-year equipment costing $100,000 in service in March 2024. It took no §179 or bonus depreciation, and the half-year convention applied. MACRS rates for 7-year property (half-year): 14.29%, 24.49%, 17.49%. What is the 2025 depreciation?

choices.explanation: That is 200% declining balance on full cost with no convention.
Correct. 2025 is the second recovery year: 24.49% × 100,000.
The half-year convention affects only the first and last years.

mcqs.explanation: The table rates already build in the half-year convention; year 2 uses 24.49% × $100,000 = $24,490.

mcqs.stem: In November 2025 a calendar-year business places $200,000 of 5-year equipment in service — its only depreciable personal property for the year. No §179 or bonus is taken. The first-year rate for 5-year property is 20% (half-year) and 5% (mid-quarter, fourth quarter). What is the 2025 depreciation?

choices.explanation: Correct. All of the year's personal property was placed in service in Q4, so the mid-quarter convention applies: 5% × 200,000.
The half-year convention is unavailable when more than 40% is placed in service in Q4.
That is a full year of 200% declining balance with no convention.
MACRS doesn't prorate by month for personal property.

mcqs.explanation: More than 40% of the year's depreciable personal property was placed in service in the last quarter, so the mid-quarter convention applies: 5% × $200,000 = $10,000.

mcqs.stem: In July 2025 an investor places a residential rental building in service. Its cost is $400,000, including $70,000 for the land. What is the 2025 depreciation?

choices.explanation: July counts as half a month under the mid-month convention, so 5.5 months, not 6.
That includes the $70,000 of land, which isn't depreciable.
That uses 39 years, the life for nonresidential real property.

mcqs.explanation: Residential rental: 27.5 years, straight-line, mid-month. Basis $330,000 ÷ 27.5 = $12,000; × 5.5/12 = $5,500.

mcqs.stem: For 2025 the §179 limit is $2,500,000, reduced dollar for dollar once qualifying property placed in service exceeds $4,000,000. A business places $4,600,000 of qualifying equipment in service and has ample business income. What is its maximum §179 deduction?

choices.explanation: The limit is reduced by the $600,000 excess over the threshold.
That is the reduction, not the remaining limit.
Subtracting the limit from the threshold isn't the phase-out rule.

mcqs.stem: A company placed 7-year equipment costing $50,000 in service in 2023 (half-year convention; no §179 or bonus) and sold it in 2025. The year-3 rate is 17.49%. What depreciation is allowed for 2025?

choices.explanation: A disposal year allows only half a year under the half-year convention.
Depreciation is allowed in the year of sale, for half a year.
Correct. In the year of disposition the half-year convention allows half of the year-3 amount: 17.49% × 50,000 × ½.
That halves the year-2 rate instead of the year-3 rate.

mcqs.explanation: Under the half-year convention, the year of disposition gets half a year: 17.49% × $50,000 × ½ = $4,373.

mcqs.stem: You are reviewing a 2025 depreciation schedule. The client placed $250,000 of 7-year equipment in service in March and $250,000 in November (no other personal property; no §179 or bonus). The preparer used the half-year rate of 14.29% on all $500,000. Mid-quarter first-year rates for 7-year property are Q1 25.00%, Q3 10.71% and Q4 3.57%. What is the correct 2025 depreciation?

choices.explanation: That is the preparer's half-year figure; mid-quarter is required.
The November equipment also gets a (small) first-year deduction.
That uses the third-quarter rate for the November assets.
Correct. 50% of the year's personal property was placed in service in Q4, so mid-quarter applies: 25% × 250,000 + 3.57% × 250,000 = 62,500 + 8,925.

mcqs.explanation: More than 40% (here 50%) of the year's personal property was placed in service in Q4, so every 2025 personal-property asset uses the mid-quarter rate for its quarter: $62,500 + $8,925 = $71,425.

mcqs.stem: A business signed a binding contract for 7-year equipment ($100,000) on January 10, 2025 and placed it in service in March 2025. What bonus depreciation is available?

choices.explanation: Correct. Property acquired before January 20 gets 40%.

mcqs.explanation: For 2025, property acquired before January 20, 2025 qualifies for 40% bonus; property acquired after January 19 qualifies for 100%.

mcqs.stem: Qualified improvement property is placed in service in 2025. What is its MACRS recovery period?
mcqs.explanation: Qualified improvement property is 15-year MACRS property eligible for bonus depreciation and §179.

mcqs.stem: Five-year equipment costing $500,000 was acquired January 5, 2025 (40% bonus). The owner elects $100,000 of §179. The half-year rate is 20%. What is total 2025 cost recovery?

choices.explanation: Add regular MACRS on the remainder.

mcqs.stem: A $100,000 seven-year asset (half-year convention) is sold in its third year. The full Year 3 rate is 17.49%. What is Year 3 depreciation?

choices.explanation: Only half a year is allowed.
Correct. Half a year in the year of disposal.

mcqs.explanation: Under the half-year convention, an asset disposed of before the end of its recovery period gets half a year of depreciation.

mcqs.stem: How is an election out of bonus depreciation made?

choices.explanation: Correct. It applies to all assets in the class.

mcqs.explanation: The bonus depreciation election out applies to all property in a recovery class placed in service that year.

mcqs.stem: A calendar-year business's only 2025 acquisition is $100,000 of 5-year equipment placed in service in November. It elects out of bonus and takes no §179. The mid-quarter Q4 first-year rate is 5%. What is 2025 depreciation?

choices.explanation: Correct. Over 40% placed in Q4 triggers mid-quarter: 100,000 × 5%.

mcqs.explanation: When more than 40% of personal property is placed in service in Q4, the mid-quarter convention applies.

mcqs.stem: A residential rental building (cost $330,000, excluding land) is placed in service in July. What is first-year depreciation under the mid-month convention?
mcqs.explanation: Residential rental property uses 27.5-year straight-line with the mid-month convention.

mcqs.stem: A nonresidential building (cost $780,000, excluding land) is placed in service in October. What is first-year depreciation?
mcqs.explanation: Nonresidential real property uses 39-year straight-line with the mid-month convention.

mcqs.stem: For 2025, the §179 limit is $2,500,000, reduced dollar for dollar once qualifying purchases exceed $4,000,000. A company places $4,300,000 of equipment in service. What is its maximum §179 deduction (before the income limit)?
mcqs.explanation: The §179 limit falls by the amount qualifying property exceeds the investment threshold.

mcqs.stem: A car is used 45% for business in 2025, its first year. Which depreciation method is required?

choices.explanation: Correct. Listed property at 50% or less business use can't use accelerated methods.

choices.text: §179 up to the luxury auto cap

mcqs.explanation: Listed property used 50% or less in business must use the alternative depreciation system.

mcqs.stem: A business buys used equipment from an unrelated seller in March 2025. Is it eligible for bonus depreciation?

choices.explanation: Correct. Used property from unrelated parties qualifies.
That isn't what the rule says.

mcqs.explanation: Bonus depreciation applies to used property the taxpayer didn't previously use, acquired from an unrelated party.

mcqs.stem: A business installs a $40,000 perimeter fence around its land. How is the cost recovered?

choices.explanation: Correct. Fencing is a land improvement.

mcqs.explanation: Land improvements such as fences and paving are 15-year MACRS property.

mcqs.stem: A buyer acquires a business and pays $90,000 for the seller's 3-year covenant not to compete. How is it amortized?

choices.explanation: Correct. Covenants in a business acquisition are §197 intangibles.

mcqs.explanation: A covenant not to compete entered into with an acquisition is a §197 intangible amortized over 15 years.

mcqs.stem: In 2025 a company pays $400,000 of domestic research wages and $100,000 of foreign research costs. How are they treated?

choices.explanation: Correct. §174A allows current deduction for domestic research.

mcqs.explanation: For tax years beginning after 2024, domestic research is deductible under §174A; foreign research stays amortized over 15 years.

mcqs.stem: A company spends $500,000 to add an elevator and enlarge an existing office building. Is it qualified improvement property?

choices.text: No, enlargements and elevators are excluded
Yes, if placed in service after 2017

mcqs.explanation: QIP is interior work on nonresidential buildings, excluding enlargements, elevators and escalators, and internal structural framework.

mcqs.stem: For property placed in service in 2025, what is the maximum §179 expense deduction?
mcqs.explanation: For 2025, the §179 limit is $2,500,000, phased out dollar-for-dollar above $4,000,000 of purchases.

mcqs.stem: What is the MACRS recovery period for residential rental property?

choices.explanation: Correct. Residential rental property uses 27.5 years.

mcqs.explanation: Residential rental property is depreciated straight-line over 27.5 years.

mcqs.stem: Which convention applies to nonresidential real property under MACRS?
mcqs.explanation: Residential and nonresidential real property use the mid-month convention.

mcqs.stem: For 2025 the §179 limit is $2,500,000, reduced dollar for dollar once qualifying property placed in service exceeds $4,000,000. A business places $4,600,000 of qualifying property in service in 2025 and has ample income. What is its maximum §179 deduction?
mcqs.explanation: Reduced dollar for dollar by purchases over $4,000,000.
mcqs.reviewNote: Uses a One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21) amount or effective date. Verify against current IRS guidance and exam materials.

mcqs.stem: A company places $500,000 of 7-year property in service in November and $300,000 in March, electing out of bonus and not using §179. Which convention applies?

choices.explanation: More than 40% was placed in service in Q4.
Not a MACRS convention for personal property.

mcqs.explanation: §168(d)(3): mid-quarter convention when more than 40% is placed in service in the last quarter.

mcqs.stem: A residential rental building (cost $550,000, excluding land) is placed in service in July. Using the mid-month convention, what is first-year depreciation?

choices.explanation: Uses 39 years with the wrong months.

mcqs.explanation: 550,000 ÷ 27.5 = 20,000 per year; July → 5.5 months.

mcqs.stem: On April 1, 2025, a company buys a business and allocates $450,000 of the price to goodwill. What is its 2025 amortization of the goodwill for tax purposes?

choices.explanation: That is a full year (450,000 ÷ 15); amortization starts in April.
Purchased goodwill is a §197 intangible and is amortizable.
Correct. §197 goodwill is amortized over 15 years (180 months) from the month acquired: 450,000 ÷ 180 × 9.

mcqs.explanation: Purchased goodwill is a §197 intangible: straight-line over 180 months beginning with the month of acquisition. $450,000 ÷ 180 × 9 = $22,500.

mcqs.stem: A self-employed consultant buys a car used 40% for business. Which cost recovery method applies?

choices.explanation: Bonus requires more than 50% business use.

choices.text: No depreciation, because it is personal use
ADS straight-line, with no §179 or bonus
choices.explanation: Correct. Listed property used 50% or less for business must use ADS straight-line.

mcqs.explanation: IRC §280F(b): listed property not predominantly (more than 50%) used for business uses the alternative depreciation system, with no §179 or bonus.

mcqs.stem: A business with $60,000 of taxable income from its active trade (before §179) elects $90,000 of §179 expense in 2025. What is its 2025 §179 deduction?

choices.explanation: Correct. §179 is limited to business taxable income; the excess carries forward.

mcqs.explanation: IRC §179(b)(3): the deduction is limited to taxable income from the active conduct of a trade or business; the excess carries forward.

flashcards.back: Annual dollar limit, reduced dollar for dollar above an investment threshold, then limited to business taxable income (excess carries forward). (The exam gives the dollar amount.)
100% for property acquired after Jan 19, 2025; 40% if acquired earlier.
More than 40% of personal property placed in service in Q4.
Residential 27.5 years; nonresidential 39 years; SL, mid-month.
